notes.name: PATH, the Pathfinder as the SMS lists it (ours, inferred: no SMS mnemonic was found)
notes.kind: the Pathfinder (AN/AAQ-20), the AN/AAQ-13 navigation pod's export version without the terrain-following radar: a forward-looking infrared camera whose picture shows on the HUD (fi-pathfinder, w-lantirn); the F-16C/D Barak's from 1992 (fi-pathfinder; which IAF jets carried it is inferred, modern-iaf/docs/research/pods.md §1). Its FLIR picture on the HUD is shared/weapons/nav_pod.gd (modern-iaf/docs/weapons.md §7.4); it has no TFR
notes.drag: as the AN/AAQ-13's (lantirn-nav.json, 0.305 m across, w-lantirn): the Pathfinder's diameter was not found (inferred)
notes.model: the AN/AAQ-13's shape (lantirn.glb, 1.99 m): no public drawing of the Pathfinder's own shape was found; it is the AN/AAQ-13 scaled down, 198 cm long (fi-pathfinder), so the stand-in is 1 cm longer (inferred)
notes.generation: ours: the weapons.ibx section key (generation · 1000 + type) is one per weapon of a kind
notes.station: the left chin hardpoint, 5L, where the F-16 carries its navigation pod (f16net-lantirn; for the Barak inferred); the sim's pylon J

footnotes.fi-pathfinder: Forecast International, Electro-Optical Systems Forecast, "Pathfinder/Sharpshooter - Archived 02/2004" (Israel's Pathfinder pods of 1992; no terrain-following radar; its FLIR on the HUD; 198 cm, 84 kg), https://www.forecastinternational.com/archive/disp_pdf.cfm?DACH_RECNO=556
footnotes.w-lantirn: Wikipedia, "LANTIRN" (the AN/AAQ-20 Pathfinder, the navigation pod's export version without the terrain-following radar; the AN/AAQ-13's 30 cm across), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LANTIRN
footnotes.f16net-lantirn: F-16.net, "AN/AAQ-13 & AN/AAQ-14 LANTIRN" (the navigation pod on 5L; the Pathfinder a derivative), https://www.f-16.net/f-16_armament_article2.html
